newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Camelot raises gold reserves at Tarmoola.
newsitem.headline: Camelot raises gold reserves at Tarmoola.

text.p: Gold producer Camelot Resources NL said on Monday it had lifted the reserve estimate for the Tarmoola gold resource in Western Australia by 53 percent to 1.52 million ounces and expected further resource increases.
Camelot and Canadian miner Teck Corp jointly own the Tarmoola mine after making a successful takeover offer for Mt Edon Gold Mines (Australia) Ltd earlier this year.

"Under Teck and Camelot's review, pit optimisations based on an increased mill throughput to 3.0 million tonnes per annum have produced a pit that contains 23.46 million tonnes at 2.01 grams per tonne (g/t) in proved and probable reserves containing 1.52 million ounces," Camelot said in a statement.
Camelot said the Tarmoola resource was now estimated to be 3.1 million ounces of gold at 1.67 g/t using a cut-off grade of 0.6 g/t, 45 percent higher than the mine's December estimate.
"Over the last nine months mill production did not reconcile well to the previous July 1996 resource model and has exceeded the gold production predicted by 34 percent," the company said.

Camelot said a pit optimisation study had identified a further 4.1 million tonnes in resources that would be added to the new reserve position if they were converted to reserves at the same tonnes and grade by infill drilling within a further optimised pit.
"These areas will be given high priority for exploration drilling," the company said.
Camelot said further exploration drilling would focus on identified extensions of the orebody and underground mining potential of the deeps mineralisation.
